title: .21 per-row tool-path coverage, RESPONSES wire (grok-4.6, Vertex xai gemini-format, xai family; the .29 session-title side-call class — observed on this wire carrying the row's body.model + store=false, rt-46c1 req-003): two headless turns in one session. Turn 1 = baseline reply (carries the MCP server announcement). Turn 2 = the coverage turn: a REAL codegraph MCP round-trip (use_tool -> codegraph__codegraph_explore against the worktree index, query 'strip_model_bound_state classify_error') AND a REAL plain tool round-trip (run_terminal_command echo), per bead apex-ayl.21. Verdict semantics (discriminating-pin design): the harness-premise pin (MCP announcement) 0-hit => BLOCKED (rig problem); the model-premise pins (use_tool issued / declared target / declared echo command — all in escaped-JSON form so the tools[] schema and the prompt cannot false-satisfy them) 0-hit => VACUOUS (the model did not take the tool path — temperament/capability gap, recorded, not a product defect); with the premises held, the round-trip and payload pins decide PASS/FAIL — and the payload proof is container-AGNOSTIC: the model must quote, in its reply, the classify_error defining file path that only the real index result carries (the prompt does not contain it; the crate is private). A 400 on the tool round-trip is NOT recovered-by-design: it FAILs as a tool-path finding. Title-side-call disclosure: the session-title side call carries the row's body.model and passes every where-filter; it cannot false-satisfy the discriminating pins (no tool arguments) and carries store=false + the row model (observed, rt-46c1 req-003), so model_f/store_f stay safe.

steps.prompt: Perform exactly these two tool calls, in this order, and no other tools: (1) use the use_tool tool to call the codegraph explore tool (qualified name codegraph__codegraph_explore) with arguments query 'strip_model_bound_state classify_error', maxFiles 2, projectPath /Users/palanisd/Projects/upstream/wt/grok-build-responses; (2) use the run_terminal_command tool to run the command: echo T21-RESP-GROK46-ECHO. After both tool results are in hand, reply with exactly three lines: line 1: T21-RESP-GROK46-DONE; line 2: the exact text the echo command printed; line 3: the repo-relative file path of the file that defines classify_error, exactly as reported in the explore result.

ndjson.label: TURN COMPLETES: the merged event stream reached the end terminal (the tool-bearing turn did not die through the responses wire).

MODEL DELIVERED: the final reply carries the DONE nonce (the model finished the turn and answered the reply protocol; the nonce is model-generated output, not prompt text, so it cannot be pre-seeded).

PLAIN ROUND-TRIP PAYLOAD (container-agnostic): the reply's line 2 carries the echo output the model read from the run_terminal_command result (the prompt names the command, so the wire grep alone cannot separate a real result from a parroted one; the sh_call discriminating pin plus this reply pin together close the loop).

MCP ROUND-TRIP PAYLOAD (container-agnostic, real-index proof): the reply's line 3 carries the classify_error defining file path as reported by the explore result. The path is NOT in the prompt and the crate is private (no training prior); the model can only produce it if the real index content flowed result -> model -> reply. 0 hits = the MCP result never carried real content (stale/empty index, wrong args, or server error) even if the call was emitted.

wire.label: CONTROL (harness premise, anti-vacuous pin): the codegraph MCP server's turn-boundary announcement ('MCP server(s) connected: - codegraph (N tools): ...') actually reached the row's wire — the rig offered the MCP tool. Pin is count-agnostic across codegraph builds (the 2026-09-14 capture read '(1 tool)', current build single-tool era; both match). 0 hits = BLOCKED/HARNESS (server never announced: startup failure, missing binary, config not inherited), not VACUOUS — no model conclusion is possible without the offer.

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): a use_tool call was actually ISSUED — the pattern is the escaped-JSON form of the tool_name key (arguments is a JSON-encoded string on the responses/cc wire), which appears only in a real function_call's arguments; the tools[] schema entry (single-level quotes) and the prompt (plain text) cannot match it. Only use_tool carries a tool_name parameter (31-tool set verified, rt-m8 req-004). 0 hits = VACUOUS.

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): a use_tool call targeted the DECLARED fully-qualified tool codegraph__codegraph_explore — the escaped-JSON form of the FQ name appears only in a real call's arguments; the prompt carries the name plain (single-level, unquoted) and the MCP announcement text carries NO FQ names at all (current codegraph build server-instructions verified: 0 'codegraph__' occurrences; the 2026-09-14 capture announce lists bare codegraph_explore). 0 hits = VACUOUS (wrong/absent target).

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): the DECLARED echo command was actually issued — the escaped-JSON form of command+value appears only in a real call's arguments (the prompt carries the command plain; the tools[] schema line is "command": {). Matches run_terminal_command or monitor with that exact command; the prompt forbids other tools, and either shell tool proves the plain builtin round-trip path. 0 hits = VACUOUS.

SHAPE (responses round-trip close): at least one function_call_output item on the row wire — a tool round-trip CLOSED (a result was produced and carried back into a later request); proves execution, not merely emission. Container-agnostic which tool closed (MCP or plain); the per-tool attribution is carried by the discriminating call pins + the reply payload pins.

MODEL ECHO (RT-M5 lineage): the NEWEST matched row request (nth=0 = newest under the runner's mtime-sorted glob) carries the row's own model id — no cross-model misrouting on the responses wire. The session-title side call also matches the where filter (same body.model), so it cannot false-fail this pin.

WIRE INVARIANT (env assumption): the NEWEST matched row request carries store=false — the deployment runs responses with store off (reasoning items are NOT persisted upstream; the XREPLAY-1 rs_ rejection class presumes it). The session-title side call also carries store=false (observed 2026-09-16, rt-46c1 req-003), so title-call interference cannot false-fail this pin.

VERDICT RECORD (evidence-only, machine-readable): the upstream HTTP status of the LAST matched row request, paired to its resp-NNN.jsonl by capture sequence. No status_in — a 400 on the tool round-trip is a tool-path FINDING surfaced by the round-trip pins (cg_rt/echo_nd/path_nd), and the session-title side call (it carries the row's body.model, so it passes the where filter; .29: it 500s proxy-side, sessions unaffected) may be the last match, so an assertive status_in would false-fail. Responses wire: the last match is normally the final turn's request; a title side call landing last records its (proxy-500) status here by design — evidence, not verdict.

vacuous_if.note: MCP server never announced on the row wire — rig failed (startup/config/binary); no model conclusion is possible without the offer. Title-call safe: the announcement is server-derived text, so a title-call hit would still prove harness MCP works.
use_tool never issued on the responses wire (escaped-form 0-hit — the tools[] schema presence of use_tool does NOT count) — model did not take the MCP-call path; probe meaningless for this cell.
no use_tool call targeted codegraph__codegraph_explore (escaped FQ-name 0-hit — the prompt's plain mention does NOT count) — the declared MCP target was never called; probe meaningless.
the declared echo command was never issued (escaped command 0-hit) — plain tool path not exercised; probe meaningless.
